title: Light and Sound
description: Light travels in straight lines and can be blocked to make shadows. Sounds are vibrations that travel through air. We use light and sound to communicate.

exercises.question: What is a SHADOW?
choices: a dark area made when an object blocks light
exercises.exp: A shadow forms when an object blocks light from passing through.

exercises.question: When is your shadow the SHORTEST?
choices: midday when the sun is high
exercises.exp: At midday the sun is directly above, so shadows are short and directly below you.

exercises.question: Which material lets NO light through? (Opaque)
exercises.exp: A wooden door is opaque — light cannot pass through it.

exercises.question: Which material lets SOME light through? (Translucent)
exercises.exp: Wax paper is translucent — it lets some light through but you cannot see clearly.

exercises.question: Sound is made when objects ___.
exercises.exp: Sound is made by vibrations — tiny back-and-forth movements that travel through air.

exercises.question: How do we use a SIREN to communicate?
choices: to signal danger or an emergency
exercises.exp: A siren uses sound to warn people of danger — like an ambulance or fire truck!

exercises.question: Light travels in ___.
exercises.exp: Light always travels in straight lines — that is why shadows have sharp edges!

exercises.question: Which of these uses LIGHT to communicate?
exercises.exp: Traffic lights use coloured light to tell drivers and walkers when to stop or go.

exercises.question: You can see yourself in a mirror because mirrors ___.
exercises.exp: Mirrors have a very smooth shiny surface that bounces (reflects) light back to your eyes.

exercises.question: Why is a clear glass window TRANSPARENT?
choices: light can pass straight through it
exercises.exp: Glass is transparent — light passes through so you can see what is on the other side.

exercises.question: A lighthouse uses LIGHT to ___.
choices: warn ships about dangers near the shore
exercises.exp: Lighthouse beams of light help ships navigate safely and avoid rocks.

exercises.question: Which of these would make the LOUDEST sound?
exercises.exp: Thunderstorms create very loud sound — the thunder can be heard far away!

exercises.question: If you move an object CLOSER to a light source, what happens to its shadow?
choices: the shadow stays the same size
exercises.exp: Moving an object closer to the light source makes the shadow LARGER — move the object away and the shadow shrinks.

exercises.question: Pluck a guitar string. It vibrates and makes a sound. If you pluck it HARDER, the sound is ___.
exercises.exp: Plucking harder makes bigger vibrations = louder sound. Plucking gently makes soft vibrations = quiet sound.

exercises.question: Which of these is a SOURCE of light?
exercises.exp: A candle flame produces its own light — it is a light source. Mirrors and the moon only REFLECT light.

exercises.question: The moon SHINES at night. Where does its light come from?
choices: the moon produces its own light
the moon reflects light from the sun
Earth shines light on the moon
exercises.exp: The moon does not make its own light — it reflects sunlight! That is why we can see it at night.

exercises.question: Sound travels through AIR. Can sound also travel through water?
choices: no, sound only travels through air
yes — sound can travel through solids, liquids, and gases
only very loud sounds can travel through water
sound cannot travel through anything but air
exercises.exp: Sound travels through all states of matter — air, water, and even solids like walls and desks!

exercises.question: You shout inside a cave and hear your voice again. This is called ___.
exercises.exp: An echo is sound reflecting off a hard surface (like cave walls) back to your ears. Sound bounces!

exercises.question: A thick curtain ABSORBS sound in a room. What does absorb mean here?
choices: the curtain soaks up sound vibrations so they do not bounce back
exercises.exp: Soft materials like curtains and carpets absorb sound — they soak up vibrations so the room is less echoey.

exercises.question: What colour is light from the SUN?
choices: white (a mix of all colours of the rainbow)
exercises.exp: Sunlight looks white but is actually a mixture of all rainbow colours. A prism splits it into red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet!

exercises.question: Which of these communicates using BOTH light and sound?
exercises.exp: A television uses both light (picture on screen) and sound (speakers) to communicate information!

exercises.question: You put your hand over a speaker and feel vibrations. This proves that ___.
choices: sound is caused by vibrations you can feel
exercises.exp: You can feel sound vibrations through touch! Speakers vibrate the air — and your hand — when they play sound.

exercises.question: Why do you SEE lightning BEFORE you HEAR thunder?
choices: thunder is quieter than lightning is bright
light travels much faster than sound
thunder travels upward and light travels downward
exercises.exp: Light travels at 300,000 km/s — sound only travels about 343 m/s. Light reaches your eyes almost instantly; sound takes longer!

exercises.question: A PRISM splits white light into a rainbow of colours. This shows that white light ___.
choices: is made of only red and blue light
is a mixture of all the colours of the visible spectrum
exercises.exp: White light is a mixture of all visible colours — a prism bends each colour differently, separating them into a rainbow!

exercises.question: Which of these is TRANSLUCENT?
exercises.exp: Frosted glass lets some light through but you cannot see clearly through it — that is translucent!

exercises.question: Dolphins and bats use SOUND to find objects around them. This is called ___.
exercises.exp: Echolocation: bats and dolphins send out sound pulses. The echoes that bounce back tell them where objects are!

exercises.question: If you stand in front of a MIRROR, your reflection ___.
choices: is always the same size as you
appears behind the mirror at the same distance you stand in front
exercises.exp: Your reflection appears to be behind the mirror at the same distance you stand in front — it is a virtual image!

exercises.question: Which of these uses SOUND to warn people of danger?
exercises.exp: A smoke alarm's loud beep is a sound signal warning people of danger — get out and call for help!

exercises.question: A shadow is LONGEST when the light source is ___.
choices: far away at a low angle (like sunrise or sunset)
exercises.exp: When the sun is low on the horizon (morning and evening), shadows stretch out very long. At noon (high sun), shadows are short.

exercises.question: Which surface makes the BEST mirror?
choices: a very smooth, shiny, polished metal surface
exercises.exp: Smooth, shiny surfaces reflect light in the same direction — creating clear reflections. Rough surfaces scatter light in all directions.

exercises.question: NOISE-CANCELLING headphones reduce unwanted sounds. They work by producing ___.
choices: louder sounds to drown out noise
sound waves that cancel out the unwanted sounds
exercises.exp: Noise-cancelling headphones produce opposite sound waves that cancel out background noise — clever sound science!

exercises.question: Light travels in ___.
exercises.exp: Light always travels in straight lines — that is why you get sharp shadows and why you cannot see around a corner!

exercises.question: Which of these is a SOURCE of light?
exercises.exp: The sun makes its own light — it is a light source. The moon only reflects sunlight; it makes no light of its own.

exercises.question: A PRISM splits white light into the colours of the rainbow. The colours in order are ___.
choices: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet
exercises.exp: A prism splits white light into seven colours: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet — remember ROY G BIV!

exercises.question: Why is the sky BLUE?
choices: the sky is made of blue gas
blue light from the sun scatters more in the atmosphere than other colours
the ocean reflects blue onto the sky
exercises.exp: Blue light has a shorter wavelength and scatters more in Earth's atmosphere — so when you look up, you see scattered blue light!

exercises.question: When sound bounces off a hard surface and you hear it again, it is called an ___.
exercises.exp: An echo is a reflection of sound. When sound hits a hard surface (like a cliff), it bounces back to your ears!

exercises.question: Which material ABSORBS sound best?
exercises.exp: Soft, porous materials like foam and fabric absorb sound waves. That is why recording studios have foam on the walls!

exercises.question: Light can bend when it passes from one material to another. This bending is called ___.
exercises.exp: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes between different materials (like air to water). It makes straws look bent!

exercises.question: You look at a spoon in a glass of water — it looks bent. This is because of ___.
choices: light refracting (bending) as it moves from water to air
exercises.exp: Light bends (refracts) when it moves from water to air at an angle — this makes the spoon appear to be in a different position!

exercises.question: The PITCH of a sound is how high or low it is. A bird chirping has ___.
choices: the same pitch as a drum
exercises.exp: Bird chirps are high-pitched sounds — they vibrate at high frequencies. A bass drum makes low-pitched sounds.

exercises.question: What happens to light when it hits a rough surface?
choices: it is reflected in one clear direction
it scatters in many different directions (diffuse reflection)
exercises.exp: Rough surfaces scatter light in many directions — this is diffuse reflection. Smooth surfaces give regular, clear reflections.

exercises.question: Which of these can light travel through?
exercises.exp: Light can travel through a vacuum — in fact, light from the sun travels through the vacuum of space to reach us!

exercises.question: During a SOLAR ECLIPSE, the moon moves between the ___.
choices: Earth and the sun, blocking sunlight
exercises.exp: In a solar eclipse, the moon passes directly between Earth and the sun — the moon's shadow falls on part of Earth!

exercises.question: The speed of light is approximately ___.
exercises.exp: Light travels at about 300,000 kilometres per second — the fastest thing in the universe! Sound is about 340 m/s.

exercises.question: Why do you see LIGHTNING before you hear THUNDER?
choices: light travels much faster than sound
your eyes are faster than your ears
exercises.exp: Light travels nearly one million times faster than sound! Lightning reaches you almost instantly; thunder travels at ~340 m/s.

exercises.question: A drum makes sound when you HIT it. The sound stops when you hold the drumhead still. This shows sound is made by ___.
exercises.exp: Sound is made by vibrations — the drumhead vibrates rapidly when hit, which vibrates the air and sends sound to your ears.

exercises.question: Which colour of light has the LONGEST wavelength?
exercises.exp: Red light has the longest wavelength in the visible spectrum. Violet has the shortest. Red → Orange → Yellow → Green → Blue → Violet.

exercises.question: A white object looks white because it ___.
choices: reflects all colours of light equally
exercises.exp: White objects reflect all colours of the visible spectrum equally — all those colours combined look white to our eyes!

exercises.question: A black T-shirt worn on a hot sunny day feels warmer than a white T-shirt. Why?
choices: black absorbs more light energy (and turns it into heat); white reflects it
exercises.exp: Black surfaces absorb more light energy and convert it to heat. White reflects most light away — staying cooler!

exercises.question: Sound travels FASTEST through ___.
exercises.exp: Sound travels fastest through solids because particles are packed tightly together and vibrations pass quickly. Steel transmits sound very fast!

exercises.question: A guitar string is plucked HARDER. The sound becomes ___.
exercises.exp: Plucking harder makes the string vibrate with a bigger amplitude — this means more energy and LOUDER sound, not higher pitch!
